title: After 6 months solo dev, I'm opening my space MMO to the public for the first time
author: valle_create
selftext:
Heyho! 👋🏼

For the past six months, I've been developing my arcade-style online space MMO, **NOVA WARP**.

Now the time has finally come: I'm opening the gates to the game for the very first time and hosting a public alpha test event.

You're warmly invited to join the alpha sessions! I'd love to see lots of you take part so we can really put the game through its paces together. Share this with your friends and test it as a group. Bosses and dungeons are designed for 3-player parties.

Waiting for you is an open-world sector system, three different player factions, 27 enemy types with unique attack patterns and abilities, various bosses, dungeons, skill tree upgrades, loot boxes, PvP, KAL the unfriendly chat moderator, and much more.

Quick note: the game currently only runs on desktop devices — so Windows, macOS, and Linux.

You can get a first look at the game here: [*https://youtu.be/oS3q03Us1\_Y*](https://youtu.be/oS3q03Us1_Y)

Save the date and sign up now at [***https://nova-warp.com***](https://nova-warp.com/) and join the Discord server.  
See you in space! 🚀

Best regards,  
Valle

comments.author: Red__Ace
comments.body:
No offense but this looks really bad.
Like tell me. Try to be unbiased for a second.
This is the first time you're looking at this game. Would you want to play this when you have AAA games? If you released this in 1980, it would still be terrible for that time to be honest. You have static images of galaxies as the background and extremely terrible sprites for spaceships and bullets. It all just looks poorly made. 

As a fellow AI developer, I can tell you this - you have wasted 6 months, drop this idea and work on something else now. What's important is what you learnt from this. 

For your next project, remember it should look attractive enough and interesting enough to make someone want to try.

replies.author: Red__Ace
replies.body:
1. How much time they spent developing it is completely irrelevant to a player. What matters is how it looks to player. This is a sunken cost fallacy

2. Unlike a keyboard warrior like yourself, I have actually shipped games and have seen the brutal reality of competition. Users make up their mind in less than 3-5 seconds about a game and it needs to impress them within that time (actual statistics). I am telling them something I have actually seen from experience; games 100 times more polished than this get buried because of the competition. 

3. I am not opposed to getting testers, but from a user POV, this is not something most users would ever even try. I can tell you that because I've studied user behavior, while you just sit there and write fake supportive comments to encourage OP to waste more time.

replies.author: Robiety101
replies.body:
Getting testers is not sunk cost fallacy, spending 6 more months on if they tell you is bad would be.  Again, I told him to get testers, not triple down.

I'm sorry your games have not done well, I assume that is where the bitterness is from. That is no OP's fault.

You clearly have anger issues and will need the last word for this to end, so I'll let you have it.  

OP, get 10 testers, let them tell you if it's any good, and go from there.

replies.author: Red__Ace
replies.body:
1. You assume I shipped games
2. You assume all my games didn't do well and not some didn't -- I learnt from my mistakes and got better result which is the whole reason I'm here giving my opinion to save OP the time it took me to learn.
3. Testers don't judge clicks or conversion. They judge if the game has bugs. For clicks and conversion, public forums are an excellent way to gauge interest.
4. Have a look at what others are building using AI. You're so disconnected from reality, it's like explaining to a layman.
5. My niche, platform and apps are completely different from OPs. It's not a competition. I shared my brutally honest opinion from both a consumer POV and a dev POV. You offered nothing to them in terms of feedback. Instead you keep insisting on testers as if testers are actual critics (very funny you keep insisting on this).
